firstPlayerRule: The player to the dealer's left takes the first turn, drawing from the stock or discard pile. With two players, the nondealer starts.
houseFallback: Bicycle does not specify the first dealer. As a house rule, choose a dealer at random, then start with the player to their left.
clarifications: Deal 10 cards each for two players, seven each for three or four, or six each for five or six.
Place undealt cards face down as the stock. Turn its top card face up to start the discard pile.
For the next hand, the previous winner deals in a two-player game. With more players, the deal moves one seat left.
These are Bicycle's basic Rummy rules; Gin Rummy and other variants have separate rules.

internalEvidence: Codex rechecked the complete Bicycle Cards Rummy (Rum) page on 2026-10-15 under the owner's request to improve affected pages. The Deal specifies 10 cards each for two players, seven for three or four, six for five or six, the face-down stock and opening discard, winner-deals for two players and leftward dealing rotation for larger groups. The Play starts with the player left of the dealer, who draws from the stock or discard pile; the two-player nondealer wording follows directly. The first dealer is not specified, so the picker remains an explicit house suggestion. The introduction distinguishes basic Rummy from Gin Rummy and other variants. Removed the unsupported 52-card assertion from the edition label: this page does not specify a pack size. Source custody: research/source-files/indexing-oct15/rummy.html; SHA-256 53d1cf6352bc2b3eaf2a1cea5b9440f6308be2eaf3aa403a290f6bbf3e5a5f76. Fixed starting position has no selection tie, and a generic card-game page does not need a boxed-game purchase suggestion. Public guidance is a concise paraphrase, not a replacement for the linked complete rules. Random-mix eligibility remains excluded.
